title: Dates and Ordinal Numbers
definition: Dates in German commonly use ordinal numbers for the day, followed by the month. Written dates often use day.month.year, for example 22.10.2026. Ordinal numbers are also used for floors, order, and birthdays.

rules.title: Ask for and give the date
rules.explanation: Ask Welches Datum haben wir heute? or Der Wievielte ist heute? A common answer is Heute ist der ...

examples.english: Today is the twenty-second of October.

examples.german: Mein Geburtstag ist am fünften Mai.
examples.english: My birthday is on the fifth of May.

rules.title: Written date format
rules.explanation: In German, the usual written order is day, month, year, with dots after the day and month numbers.

rules.title: Ordinal numbers
rules.explanation: From 1 to 19, ordinal numbers commonly take -te; from 20 onward they commonly take -ste. Some forms are irregular and should be memorized.

rules.title: Dates with am
rules.explanation: When giving the date of an event, am is followed by the dative form of the ordinal number, commonly ending in -ten or -sten.

rules.title: Birthdays and invitations
rules.explanation: Use Geburtstag for birthday and Wann hast du Geburtstag? to ask when someone's birthday is.

examples.german: Ich habe am zwölften August Geburtstag.
examples.english: My birthday is on the twelfth of August.

common_mistakes.explanation: After am, the ordinal takes the dative ending -en.

mastery_goal: You can read and say common dates, ask about birthdays, and use basic ordinal numbers with am.
